Inspect sticky privacy-release services

Source: R/privacy.R
ds.omop.dp.status.Rd

Queries every selected DataSHIELD server. Unlike permissive exploration helpers, this function never returns a partial federation: each requested node must provide a well-formed status.

Usage

ds.omop.dp.status(datasources = NULL)

Arguments

datasources

Named DataSHIELD connection list. NULL uses DSI::datashield.connections_find().

Value

An omop_dp_status named list of per-server DP status records.

Details

dsOMOP 2.10.3 uses the protected-release contract: canonical fixed-basis or realised-contribution components, without history-based admission or stored answers. This client declares that contract in its status request; the new server refuses clients 2.10.2 and earlier with an upgrade message. Every older server is explicitly warned as unpatched. Installing the new client cannot repair server-side disclosure defects. Mixed old/new protected pooling is refused; per-site results remain labelled by contract.

On servers 2.10.0 to 2.10.2 the v3 service is seed-only: release_binding = "seed_data_versioned_v1", persistent_state = "noise_root_only", service_capacity = "none" and history_dependent = FALSE. Every answer is a deterministic function of the server's secret root, the question, the protected statistic and a private automatic database version, so it is identical after restarts and on every R server sharing the root, and a reload that adds rows re-draws every answer at once. Servers 2.7.1 to 2.9.x report history-dependent first-answer binding instead: persistent_state = "noise_root_and_release_bindings", release_binding = "snapshot_first_answer_v1", and service_capacity = "public_identity_reservations_v1". They retain one complete answer per public request, snapshot and privacy epoch until the custodian rotates the snapshot or epoch. Both contracts are accepted, also mixed in one federation. There is no lifetime privacy budget or privacy call quota. Epsilon, the privacy epoch and the secret root remain server-owned. Legacy v2 status is inspectable and printed as legacy. Release calls require v3 by default. During a staged upgrade, options(dsomop.dp.allow_legacy_servers = TRUE) permits v2 releases, including mixed federations, with a warning naming each legacy server. The old contract has no first-answer binding: an unrotated data refresh can reveal whether a released statistic changed; see isglobal-brge/dsOMOP#20. The release result records every site's contract. Eligible input frames must also carry the server's authenticated person-local provenance capsule; a copied class or plain attribute is not sufficient. DP concerns only the OHDSI community tools: connecting, loading tables, filters, factors and dsOMOP's own exploration never use it. Since server 2.8.0, exclusive is FALSE by default and, when a custodian sets it, applies only to the community tools (servers 2.7.x applied it to standard statistics). A missing exclusive field on older servers is treated as FALSE. Servers 2.9.0 and later also report tools_mode, the community tools' protection mode ("auto" by default, "standard" or "dp"). Status may contain a public snapshot_id label. Federated sites may report different labels. On 2.10.3 servers it is optional display metadata with no effect on admission or noise. Fixed synopses are keyed on a private person-membership generation recomputed within each request's database snapshot, without a per-session cache. Clinical-value updates that leave person membership unchanged do not change that generation; cross-version inference remains a residual. The public data_generation, data_generation_basis and data_generation_residual fields describe the policy without revealing the private generation. Protected pooling across multiple sites requires distinct payload identifiers source$logical_source_id; missing or repeated identifiers are refused, while per-site results remain available. On legacy servers only, release preflight rejects repeated noise_domain_id or server-owned logical domain values.

Examples

if (FALSE) ds.omop.dp.status() # \dontrun{}
